newsitem.title: ESTONIA: SAS Estonia row may halt flights.
newsitem.headline: SAS Estonia row may halt flights.

text.p: Estonian aviation officials and negotiators from Scandinavia on Wednesday failed to solve a row over routes between the Baltic state, Denmark and Sweden which may mean these flights have to be suspended, officials said.
"During these talks, an agreement that would satisfy both sides was not reached," the Estonian Civil Aviation Service said in a statement after a second day of talks to end the deadlock.
"As long as there is no final decison, the air connection on these routes may stop from November 16," the statement added.
The talks were taking place as a November 15 deadline for confirming the airlines' winter schedule looms.
The row began after Estonian Air, majority-owned by Danish Maersk, itself owned by A.P. Moeller, said it wanted to resume flights to Copenhagen.
It asked Scandinavian Airlines to cut its flights to the Danish capital to one a day from two.
The Estonian Civil Aviation Authority has so far also refused to grant SAS permission to fly twice a day to Stockholm from Tallinn to match Estonian Air's twice-daily flights to the Swedish capital.

"We had five compromise versions but we failed and it is very unclear what will happen from November 16 on the Tallinn/Copenhagen route when present agreements end," Estonian Civil Aviation Administration head Eduard Tuur told Reuters.
"We have a couple of days, I hope a settlement can be reached," he added.

SAS says these routes should be considered as one question and that each airline would have three flights each between Estonia, Sweden and Denmark. The Estonians want to consider the routes as two separate issues.
SAS is also involved in a row in Latvia, where it owes a large stake in Air Baltic, over flights between Moscow and Riga.
